purpose: This cream is used to soften, smooth, and remove very dry, rough, thickened, or scaly skin. It is commonly used for conditions like very dry heels, calluses, corns, eczema, psoriasis, and thickened nails. It helps your skin hold onto moisture and breaks down tough, hardened skin so it can heal better.
how_it_works: Urea is a natural substance that your body already makes, and when used on your skin in high amounts, it works in two helpful ways. First, it acts like a sponge, pulling moisture into the skin and locking it in so skin stays hydrated. Second, it gently loosens and dissolves the bonds holding dead, hardened skin cells together, so that thick or crusty skin can soften and peel away naturally.
common_side_effects: Some people may notice a mild stinging, burning, or itching feeling right after applying it, especially if skin is cracked or irritated. You might also notice some redness or a slight rash at the spot where it is applied. These effects are usually mild and go away quickly as your skin gets used to the cream.
warnings: Do not use this cream inside your eyes, mouth, nose, or any other body openings. Avoid putting it on skin that is very broken, deeply cut, or seriously infected without asking your doctor first. Keep it away from children's reach, and if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, check with your doctor before using it. If you notice severe burning, swelling, or a serious rash, stop using it and contact your healthcare provider right away.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer of this cream to the affected area of skin usually once or twice a day, or as directed by your doctor or pharmacist. Rub it in gently until it is absorbed. Wash your hands after applying it unless your hands are the area being treated. Use it regularly for best results, and do not use more than recommended.
